summary: The page is a working 3D boot-packing tool with an editable rectangular boot measured in centimeters, several differently sized bags, drag and rotate controls, geometric overlap/outside warnings, and a live fitting-bag count. Desktop and mobile layouts, multiple camera views, boundary and recovery flows, reload, and runtime diagnostics were tested successfully.

runtime.reason: The Trunkfit page loaded and rendered its interactive 3D scene and controls. A reload returned document.readyState 'complete' and restored the initial 120 x 82 x 52 cm, 3/3 clear state. Runtime diagnostics recorded no console errors or warnings, and all page, font, and Three.js requests succeeded with 200 or 304 responses.

scene.reason: The central scene is genuine task-relevant 3D: the rectangular boot has perspective, floor grid, height labels, side walls, floor shadows, and occlusion between three distinct bag meshes. The 3/4, Top, and orbited views reveal consistent depth and spatial relationships rather than a static image.

checks.reason: The default 3/4 view, Top view, and an orbited perspective all showed the same boot and three bags with coherent volume, depth, occlusion, floor contact, and changing projection. Warning outlines also stayed aligned to bag geometry.

The layout has a clear three-panel hierarchy on desktop and a readable stacked mobile composition. Warm bag colors, teal clear-state cues, red issue cues, soft shadows, large headings, and compact measurements make the fit status and selected bag easy to identify.

Rotating the selected bag changed its silhouette and produced immediate fit warnings; dragging it changed the displayed X/Z position and relocated the 3D geometry; editing width resized the boot and updated the fit conditions. All feedback was visible in the scene, labels, issue counter, and bag count.

The 90-degree turn reversed with the opposite turn control, a 70 cm width created a boundary failure state, Reset bags restored the starting layout with confirmation, the Estate preset restored the original dimensions, and reload returned the full app to 3/3 fit.

Desktop at 1440x900 and mobile at 390x844 were both readable and usable. On mobile the 1,530 px page scrolled to the below-fold boot editor, its Hatch preset remained clickable, Tab placed a visible 2 px focus ring on the rotate-left control, and reload recovered cleanly. Console had 0 messages and all network resources loaded with 200/304 responses; real touch hardware was not tested.

The initial page shows a rectangular 3D boot with editable Width, Depth, and Height fields labeled in cm, plus three visibly different bags measured as 68 x 30 x 46 cm, 54 x 26 x 38 cm, and 50 x 28 x 26 cm. The mobile layout preserves the same cm fields and quick presets.

The Turn 90 button changed the selected Grand Tourer from a wide to a depth-oriented silhouette. Dragging the bag changed its displayed X/Z from -17/-25 to -15/29 and visibly moved the orange mesh across the bay, with the fit calculation updating in the same response.

Rotating the Grand Tourer immediately labeled it OUTSIDE and produced an OVERLAP with the Carry-on, reducing fit to 1/3. Drag placement produced three outside/overlap flags, and narrowing the boot to 70 cm marked all three bags outside at 0/3 while the bag-volume readout remained 184 L, demonstrating placement-based rather than volume-only validation.

The count changed from 3/3 initially to 1/3 after rotation, 0/3 after dragging a bag outside and after shrinking the boot to 70 cm, then back to 3/3 after Reset bags and after reload. Each count matched the per-bag FITS/OUTSIDE labels and issue count.

instruction.reason: Every stated requirement is delivered coherently: editable centimeter boot dimensions, three differently sized bags, move and turn interactions, geometric overlap/outside warnings including rotated cases, and a live fitting-bag count that does not rely on total volume alone.

spatial.reason: Shapes, scale, depth, occlusion, lighting, and the rectangular boot boundary consistently support the fit task across the 3/4, top, and orbited views. Bag placement and warning outlines align with the rendered geometry.

interaction.reason: Required actions, combinations, reverse rotation, boundary edits, reset recovery, presets, and keyboard focus all worked reliably. The scene, selected measurements, per-bag badges, issue count, and fit total updated together without recovery problems.

visual.reason: Composition, typography, color, materials, shadows, and state transitions consistently improve comprehension. The selected bag, warning boxes, outside/overlap labels, clear-state badge, and measurements remain legible on desktop and mobile.

stability.reason: Standard, repeat, boundary, mobile, focus, and reload checks remained usable and readable. Console diagnostics were empty and all resources loaded successfully; two transient MCP wait timeouts recovered and did not indicate an application failure.

limitations: No export or download control was advertised or visible, so exported-image inspection was not applicable.
The 390x844 viewport was exercised with Playwright mouse and keyboard input; real touch hardware behavior was not certified.
One screenshot request and one reload wait timed out at the tool layer, but both recovered on retry and later screenshots plus console/network diagnostics confirmed the page remained responsive.
The visible Add bag and remove-bag controls were not exercised because the requested checks were fully covered by the existing three bags, placement edits, and boot resizing.
